checks.rule: A title plan supports the property description in the register and identifies the general extent of registered land.
A title plan must be read together with the register rather than as a standalone exact-boundary source.
All title plans show general boundaries unless a boundary is shown as determined under section 60.
New title plans are based on the information in the title deeds and Ordnance Survey mapping current at registration.
Do not promote title-plan red edging as a surveyed exact legal boundary unless determined-boundary evidence exists.
Typical title-plan scale is 1:1250 in urban areas and 1:2500 in rural areas.
Large rural title plans may use 1:5000 or 1:10000 scales.
Registered land is usually shown by red edging following physical or plotted undefined boundary lines.
Measurements shown from deeds can indicate boundary position but the title plan still shows only a general boundary.
Treat old deed dimensions cautiously because reference points or features may have disappeared or changed.
Title plans can contain references for easements, covenants and land removed from the title.
Do not assume a title plan is current survey geometry because title plans are not routinely updated when OS mapping changes.
